correctness.rationale: For any M>=2 finite conserved classical phase sectors and positive weights, a fresh-preparation unconditional interval channel has offdiagonal factor gamma(dt)=sum_s p_s exp(-2i omega_s dt), and pairwise vanishing for K time points makes K unit vectors in C^M orthonormal, so K<=M. At K=M, expanding Tr[(VV*)^2] and bounding by diagonal entries of V*V proves average squared offdiagonal visibility at least (M sum p_s^2-1)/(M-1), with equal-step Fourier phase choices attaining equality for any weights. Full pairwise zero at K=M implies p_s uniform because V unitary; for regularly spaced times, geometric sums force phases to be the rotated Mth roots, giving converse. For N=M-1 intervals with one static label retained, the normalized process Choi state is a mixture of N-fold pure-state tensor powers; Fourier averaging kills offdiagonal Dicke sectors 0..N and yields eigenvalues 2^{-N}binom(N,k). Full computational-leg dephasing has 2^N equally weighted diagonal entries; hence coherence N ln2 - H(Bin(N,1/2)) and asymptotic N ln2-1/2 ln(pi eN/2)+o(1). Check physical Ising spectrum for M=2^r and M=4 coherence 3/4 ln3. Independent numerical matrices corroborated M=2,3,4,8; analytic Gram/Dicke calculations prove the general case. Conditioning on selected previous outcomes is explicitly excluded.
